column1: # Terminal-residue frequencies of peptides per protease / ligand class, for the FASTag tag-profile call
# (external.protease_call). Taken from public data; nothing fitted on prose-auto test runs. I and L merged.
# C = peptide C-terminal residue (protease P1), N = peptide N-terminal residue (P1'); background = proteome composition.
#   modified 2022-11-25), protein substrates only (no synthetic or theoretical cleavages): Trypsin S01.151 (22940 sites),
#   proteasome XT01.001 (879). Arg-C C11.001 (7 sites) and Asp-N M72.001 (19) are listed but too thin: their models are
#   the PeptideCutter rules (after R; before D) with the background at the other end (see external.py).
# atlas:* = MHC Motif Atlas ligand ends (http://mhcmotifatlas.org/data/classI/MS/Peptides/all_peptides.txt and
#   .../classII/..., downloaded 2026-11-02), alleles weighted equally: HLA-I 127 human alleles, 447548 ligands
#   (neutral mass median 1080 Da, q95 1358 Da); HLA-II 82 human DR/DP/DQ alleles, 548858 ligands (median 1817 Da).
# background = UniProt human reference proteome (the panel Homo_sapiens.fasta).
# Resolved for FASTag -digest_models: model names are final, class = enzyme value for the runner-up rule;
# Arg-C/Asp-N/unspecific already expanded; background = mixing component (share 0.05), not a model.
